prompt: Assess whether the evidence in the context is sufficient to confirm maturity level 3 for "Governance, Security and Ethics". Identify the gap (if any) and recommend the next concrete step.
context:
AI Maturity — Governance, Security and Ethics — excerpt from a client diagnostic interview:
"The company formalizes its AI approach. Project approval processes, risk assessment criteria, and dedicated roles (AI Officer/Committee) are introduced. Models are versioned and audited. AI is not deployed without formal approval."

The team says this reflects digital maturity level 3 of 5 ("Organization-Wide AI Governance Framework").

binaryCriteria.description: Does not accept the client self-report at face value; explicitly asks for a concrete, checkable artifact before confirming the maturity level.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Satisfied if the answer requests something like: Evidence: an AI project register with columns: description, risk assessment, decision-maker, approval date, status. An AI Committee charter or a description of the AI Officer role. A model repository (MLflow) with versi…

binaryCriteria.description: Identifies a concrete, correct next step or defensive move consistent with the next maturity stage (or, for a top-level claim, a concrete way to defend/extend it) — not a generic "digitize more" platitude.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Must name a specific mechanism, system, or practice, not a vague call to "improve digitally".

binaryCriteria.description: The recommendation is grounded in the specifics of the client's described current practice, not a copy-paste generic maturity answer that ignores the actual tools/process mentioned in the context.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer could be pasted unchanged into any other maturity area without modification.

goldNotes:
Expert verification probes: Does the organization have formal AI project approval processes — with a use-case register, risk assessment and required approval before deployment? | Is there a dedicated role or committee (AI Officer, AI Committee) responsible for AI governance in the company? | Are AI models versioned and audited — i.e. is it known which model version is running in production and when it was last checked?
What satisfies the evidence bar: Evidence: an AI project register with columns: description, risk assessment, decision-maker, approval date, status. An AI Committee charter or a description of the AI Officer role. A model repository (MLflow) with version history for production models.
Next level (4, "Continuous AI Risk Management & Monitoring"): The organization has a structured, continuous AI control system. This includes real-time model monitoring, drift detection, and security testing. AI is treated as seriously as mission-critical systems.
Relevant technology categories: AI Governance Platform (IBM OpenScale, Fiddler AI), MLflow Model Registry, GRC Tool (AI risk), AI Committee Charter Template
domain: AI Maturity — Governance, Security and Ethics
